proof: BETA-09 closes the backend maintenance-compatibility gap without shipping Studio: the generated App requires a host-owned maintenance Authority decision, every durable command carries a bounded audited reason, stale callers receive the settled winner version, and questpie.internal.v5 upgrades the append-only audit catalog from v4 without accepting checksum drift.

acceptanceCriteria: The generated CreateAppInput requires maintenance.authorize, the generated application passes it to the durable surface, and there is no implicit allow, ambient Admin/System Principal, browser client, Fetch route, or Operation-Wire maintenance transport.

Maintenance Authority is evaluated for the trusted Principal, exact command, and run identity before the target row is locked; a denied caller receives typed AUTHORITY_DENIED and the attempt is recorded with actor and reason in the append-only audit.
acknowledgeAmbiguity, cancelRun, and retryRun each require a reason of 1 through 256 characters; invalid input is a typed, audited REASON_INVALID result and does not mutate the run.

Expected-version fencing refuses a stale caller with VERSION_MISMATCH and returns the settled current run version, which can be used for a successful retry; every applied or rejected outcome reports the settled version.

questpie.internal.v5 adds the nullable bounded maintenance reason to the existing append-only audit catalog, installs fresh or upgrades v4 in the pinned protocol transaction, and refuses a same-version checksum mismatch without partially accepting drift.
The generated Runtime Build declares questpie.internal.v5 and the runtime artifact decoder retains v4 compatibility while accepting and requiring the v5 build for newly compiled applications.

The maintenance tests include a positive-controlled instrument proving denial precedes FOR UPDATE, PostgreSQL evidence for audited denial and authorized success, all three invalid-reason paths, winner-version recovery, and durable write-guard re-arming.
The reference-local performance test executes 20 fenced maintenance commands and records 20 audit rows under the 400 ms budget without increasing the accepted BETA-07 server-bundle budget.

Studio UI, browser mounting, an inspection read model, a failed-run worklist, and ambient privileged authority remain explicit non-goals; drain remains Runtime lifecycle rather than a fourth durable maintenance command, and the public guide makes no unsupported Studio, retention, or Runtime-limit claim.
